title: Chameleon-SAT: An Adaptive Boolean Satisfiability Accelerator Using Mixed-Signal In-Memory Computing for Versatile SAT Problems
problem: Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problems have diverse scales and complexity; existing SAT solvers cannot efficiently handle the full spectrum with variable solution requirements (completeness, speed).
motivation: SAT is NP-complete and fundamental to data-intensive applications; different problem classes require different algorithmic approaches, making a single general-purpose solver insufficient.
method: Chameleon-SAT is a specialized computer chip (an ASIC) that solves Boolean satisfiability problems—puzzles where you find true/false values satisfying a set of logical rules. It uses mixed-signal in-memory computing (calculations done directly in memory using both digital and analog signals) to run three different solving strategies: local search (making small changes to find solutions), DPLL (systematic exploration with backtracking), and CDCL (learning from conflicts to avoid repeating failed attempts). By reconfiguring to use the best strategy for each problem's type and size, it efficiently handles the full range from small high-complexity cases to large high-complexity problems.
key_novelty: Chameleon-SAT is the first ASIC that can adaptively switch between three satisfiability-solving strategies (local search, DPLL, and CDCL) using mixed-signal in-memory computing.
contributions: ASIC-based SAT accelerator with mixed-signal in-memory computing
Support for local search, DPLL, and CDCL algorithm classes
Adaptive reconfiguration for problem-specific optimization: 90x speedup (small/high-complexity), 19x (medium/structured), 7x (large/high-complexity)
primary_theme: Adaptive ASIC SAT accelerator with in-memory computing
